newsitem.title: DUBAI: Around 1,500 Iraqi pilgrims arrive in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Around 1,500 Iraqi pilgrims arrive in Saudi.

text.p: Some 1,000 Iraqis arrived in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday to perform haj, the first from Iraq to perform the annual Moslem pilgrimage to Mecca since 1994, a Saudi official said.
The pilgrims arrived at the Saudi city of Arar on the border with Jordan in a convoy of 27 buses at dawn, he told Reuters by telephone from the kingdom.

Iraq stopped sending pilgrims to the haj in 1995, saying U.N. trade sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait had emptied its coffers. Some 500 Iraqis travelled to Saudi Arabia for the 1994 haj.
Iraq, with population of 20 million, can send up to 20,000 pilgrims to Mecca under quotas set by the Organisation of the Islamic Conference.
But officials said financial constraints forced authorities to limit the number to about 1,000 this year. Every pilgrim is allowed to carry $500 with him.
Pleas by Iraq to have part of its assets frozen abroad released for haj purposes went unheeded.

The United Nations also rejected a request by Iraq to use its planes to fly pilgrims to Saudi Arabia. The embargo bans air and sea links with Iraq, leaving Jordan as the main overland route for Iraqis.
Some two million Moslems perfom the haj which reaches its climax on Wednesday.
